limitations: One repetition per agent arm in each run; fixed model ID, stochastic inference and provider-side revisions uncontrolled. No stable overall app speed or quality improvement established.
Same predeclared 30 eligible tasks in both runs; all 66 attempts retained, including the three excluded reference-conflict tasks.
Fresh reader processes, one host, three operation repetitions, uncontrolled OS file cache; RSS is peak for one worker or subprocess, not aggregate memory.
Agent timing includes inference and agent tools but excludes external benchmark grading and native Excel evaluation.
Both terminal images lack a formula engine. Updated helper engine invocation is tested separately on the host; this is not integrated Docker calculation or Electron UI proof.
Package plus skill and helper changes are measured together; no package-only attribution.

Guard use is instruction-based. Declared ranges must match user intent; agents can omit the guard or deliver after rejection. A passing guard does not prove expected values or that a requested formula is present, and is not bound to the final output hash.

Raw outputs are graded for preservation and formatting; independently evaluated Excel copies provide formula values. Formula-containing output copies are opened in native Excel; value-only outputs are parsed without a native UI open check.
Thirty unchanged golden evaluations are reused only after source and evaluated hashes and Excel version were verified; golden self-check is rerun.
Native content-recovery prompts are declined and counted as invalid outputs. LibreOffice grades are a separate interoperability comparison.
Provider cost is unavailable. Token sums include only records with reported totals; missing timeout totals are not zero usage.
Scores use reviewed answer regions, explicitly requested styles, formulas, structure and preservation; they are not official leaderboard scores. Failure groups overlap.

Observed SheetOps commands include reads and verify-edits; edits use agent-authored Python. Task failures do not establish a SheetOps write API defect. Future-sheet macro behavior, VBA execution and every unsupported workbook feature are not certified.
